title: Operator snooping guard, KMS token scrubber, and residency signer
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds operator-snooping-guard middleware, KMS token scrubber, and residency-signer for audit provenance. No customer-facing API changes; rollout behind feature flag.
description:
Context and motivation: This PR implements three coordinated controls to harden cross-tenant operator access, ensure KMS request metadata is not leaked to logs, and produce a signed residency assertion attached to audit events. Motivation came from an internal review (SEC-88) and a support escalation (SUP-3214) where operator-assisted recoveries could surface sensitive KMS origin headers and ambiguous residency markers in logs. Goals: 1) prevent operator console / support tooling from seeing raw tenant KMS tokens or service account tokens (operator snooping guard), 2) sanitize all KMS authorization material before passing to audit pipelines (KMS token scrubber), 3) emit a concise, signed residency assertion that can be attached to audit events and used by downstream policy evaluators (residency signer).

Summary of changes: - Introduces operator-snooping-guard HTTP middleware that enforces RBAC-v2 decisions for operator-scoped requests, blocking or masking fields if the operator principal lacks explicit read scope for tenant-sensitive headers. The middleware consults the policy cache and falls back to a synchronous policy fetch only on cache miss. - KMS token scrubber: central filter in the audit-proxy which replaces Authorization and X-KMS-Origin headers with stable redacted placeholders and emits a scrubbed_sample to the audit payload. Scrubbing is pluggable by provider (aws/gcp/azure) and configurable per-tenant residency policy. - Residency signer: small service that signs a canonical JSON assertion containing region_pin, kms_provider, and token_scope_hash using a cluster-local signing key (KMS-backed). The signed assertion is attached to the audit envelope as residency_assertion and stored in the audit stream for downstream verification. - Adds unit and integration tests for middleware, scrubber, and signer; adds end-to-end test that exercises operator console flow, ensuring scrubbed headers are not present in operator-accessible logs. - Feature flag gate: security.operator_snoop_guard (disabled in prod by default until rollout plan completes).

Checklist (from author): - [x] Design doc: linked in PR description (Linear ENG-5421) - [x] Unit tests for scrubber and signer - [x] Integration test for operator console flow - [x] Load-test smoke to confirm latency overhead < 2ms p50 - [x] Feature flag added and documented - [x] Documentation: added runtime-config entry and rollout notes

Commits (high-level): - Maya Chen: add operator snooping guard middleware and tests - Maya Chen: implement kms token scrubber and provider adapters - Maya Chen: residency signer + signing key bootstrap integration tests - Diego Alvarez: fix policy cache race found during review - Aisha Patel: update telemetry and tracing spans

Files changed (high-level): - services/gateway/middleware/operator_snoop_guard.go (new) - services/audit/proxy/scrubber.go (new) - services/audit/signer/residency_signer.go (new) - internal/policy/cache.go (touched) - config/feature_flags.yaml (touched) - test/e2e/operator_snoop_flow_test.go (new) - docs/security/operator_snoop_guard.md (new) - deployments/helm/values-security.yaml (touched) - scripts/bootstrap_signing_key.sh (new) - ci/pipeline/security_checks.yml (touched) - observability/metrics/README.md (touched)

Review thread (condensed): - Diego Alvarez (reviewer): "Overall direction looks good. Two asks: make the scrubber deterministic for reproducible audit deltas and please add a knob to retain redacted originals for delayed forensic retrieval behind a strict access guard." Maya: "Added deterministic hashing for scrub placeholders and a 'forensics_retention' config that writes encrypted originals to a restricted S3 bucket (access audited). See scrubber provider adapters." Diego: Approved after follow-up commit. - Aisha Patel (reviewer): "Concerned about policy cache staleness causing false denies for live operator workflows." Maya: "Cache TTL default is 30s; added forced synchronous fallback path and metrics for cache_misses and fallback_latency. Also added a migration note in docs." Aisha: "LGTM after tests." - Connor McBride (approver): "Please ensure the signing key bootstrap script is idempotent for private deployments." Maya: "Script updated to be idempotent and to log safe warnings on first-run. Added verification test." Connor: Approved.

CI matrix and outcomes: - unit-tests: pass - integration-tests (audit): pass - load-smoke: pass (p50 overhead < 1.5ms, p99 < 6ms) - lint: pass - security-scan (dependency-check): pass after bumping a transitive parquetlib dep that caused a warning - e2e: flaky at first due to race; fixed by increasing test harness wait for policy propagation; final run: pass

Rollout and operational notes: - Feature is behind security.operator_snoop_guard flag. We plan a staged rollout: enable on internal-only tenant pool for 72h -> enable on low-traffic dev customers -> enable for all non-enterprise tenants -> enterprise tenants by opt-in. - Telemetry: metrics added: security.snoop_guard.cache_miss_total, security.scrubber.redacted_total{provider,tenant}, security.residency.sign_requests_total, security.residency.verify_failures_total. Alerts proposed in console runbook. - Forensics path: when forensics_retention is enabled, scrubber stores encrypted originals to a tenant-specific S3 prefix with strict bucket policies and an operator access workflow that requires a second approver. - Backwards compatibility: no changes to public API surfaces; audit envelope extended with residency_assertion which downstream consumers should ignore if unknown.

Security considerations: - The signing key is provisioned via KMS and never exported. We added a CI gating check that ensures signing key references are not present in PR diffs. - The scrubber uses a deterministic HMAC with tenant-scoped master key to prevent correlation cross-tenant while keeping placeholders reproducible for dedupe. - RBAC: operator-snooping-guard enforces RBAC-v2 attribute checks; we added a policy simulator to test common operator flows and a small migration guide for teams that rely on operator-level visibility.

Merge outcome: Merged via squash on 2024-12-03 after approvals from Diego, Aisha, and Connor. Release note entry added to CHANGELOG under Unreleased -> Security.
